messages:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME opened a Zendesk (#12345) — after we rolled the new failover policy they started seeing intermittent 401s and large latency (5-12s). They believe some requests are still hitting eu-west even though their app is pinned to us-east. Logs attached below.
jon_eng: Can you paste the request id + sample headers? Also which commit rolled the policy?
maria_support: request_id=01f7a3e2, ts=2026-03-15T13:12:04Z. Headers snippet:
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Client-Region: us-east-1
Authorization: Bearer tok_xxx
Cookie: _rwd_affinity=eu-west-1; Path=/; Max-Age=604800
```
They got a 401 with auth log: `aud mismatch (expected: us-east-1, got: eu-west-1)` and a token validation latency ~110ms extra.
li_devops: Aha — looking at the deployed policy YAML, it was authored like this (from infra repo @rev a3b9):
```
failover_policies:
  - region: eu-west-1
    weight: "20%"
    priority: "1"
    sticky: true
  - region: us-east-1
    weight: "80%"
    priority: "0"
    sticky: false
```
Note: weights are strings with `%` and priority is string. Parser expects numeric weights (0-1 float) and priorities as increasing integers (lower=preferred). Our parser was permissive and normalized the weights by stripping non-numeric then dividing by 100, but because sticky=true on eu-west it created affinity cookies with region tag and long TTL, so even when us-east was preferred the cookie kept routing to eu-west.
jon_eng: So two issues: (1) percentage strings were accepted and normalized in a way that wasn't obvious in the UI, (2) sticky on the non-primary region caused stale affinity. Any evidence the affinity cookie is honored across region fallback? That cookie is decrypted by runtime and includes region id.
li_devops: Yes — runtime code sets `_rwd_affinity` when sticky=true on whichever node served the initial request. The cookie TTL was set to 7d. Because our priority comparator treats lower numeric priority as higher precedence, having priority: "0" for us-east actually made it preferred (that's fine), but the policy ordering got swapped in the console display (we render ascending instead of by explicit priority) which confused infra-author. So authors thought eu-west was primary.
kevin_sre: Impact: existing sessions got pinned to eu-west via cookie -> token audience mismatch ->401s. Latency spike likely from cross-region auth checks and KV cache misses. Recommended immediate mitigations:
- Ask customer to clear `_rwd_affinity` cookie (workaround)
- Patch console to show explicit priority sorting and warn when sticky=true on non-primary
- Short-term: roll runtime tweak to ignore affinity cookie when token aud doesn't match region (fast failover)
jon_eng: For repro we should simulate: create token with aud=us-east-1, hit eu-west with cookie set -> expect 401. Can repro locally with curl:
```
curl -v -H "Cookie: _rwd_affinity=eu-west-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-aud-us-east-1>" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
maria_support: Provided that to customer as repro steps. Customer confirmed clearing cookie fixed immediate errors but they want us to ensure stable routing. They've asked for a postmortem and ETA on the fix.
li_devops: Action items I propose:
- Short-term (hotfix): runtime: when cookie region != token aud, prefer token aud and ignore cookie (safe heuristic). Patch and deploy to hosted tonight. (owner: li_devops)
- UI: make weights accept both floats and percentages but normalize and surface exact numeric values and validation errors (owner: jon_eng)
- Console UX: show explicit priority sorting and add a warning badge when sticky=true on non-primary region (owner: ux-team ticket)
- Customer comms: maria_support to send workaround & ETA
kevin_sre: Also file an incident if we see >0.5% of requests with aud mismatch across regions in next 24h. I can add a metric and alert.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-145 (linked)
maria_support: I'll send the note to ACME and ask them to clear cookies and confirm once done. Thanks all :heart:
jon_eng: I'll open PRs for the parser normalization and the runtime heuristic. Will add unit tests for percent and float parsing & cookie precedence.
